newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares slip as Arab Bank eases.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares slip as Arab Bank eases.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange eased for a second day on Monday as demand for blue-chip stocks was undermined by a fall in market-moving Arab Bank shares.
The Amman market's official 60-share index shed 0.10 percent to 167.44 points in trade worth 1.27 million dinars ($1.8 million).

Arab Bank shares, which are heavily weighted on the official share index and have pushed it up to three-year highs this week, fell back two dinars to 293 dinars in relatively quiet turnover of under 180,000 dinars.
Brokers say Arab Bank is enjoying a good year and expectations of a bonus share offering are also boosting demand.

But the bank's shares got their biggest boost over the last couple of weeks from the announcement of government plans to scrap foreign share ownership ceilings. The foreign investor stake in the bank is already over the 50 percent legal limit.
The Jordanian cabinet has yet to formally endorse the scrapping of ownership ceilings.
"The shares are not going to move far until the cabinet approves or rejects the proposal," said analyst Mohammad Abdallah of Pearl Consultants.

Jordan Islamic Bank, which has also reached its 50 percent maximum foreign share ownership, rose 0.05 dinars to 3.98 in healthy turnover on Monday. Jordan Cement Factory rose 0.04 dinars to 4.05 on foreign and local demand.
Overall 18 shares rose on Monday and 16 fell, with another nine trading but closing unchanged.

The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance, shed 0.04 percent on Sunday to 81.33 points. It is still 2.48 percent down from the start of the year. $1 = 0.709 dinars
